description:
FILED s405 (Opus 5) from the #346/#358 work; standing ruled s406 (plan-post-s400 §2c interim): BEHIND THE RELEASE unless it turns out to be a one-line :preserve-fds widening — it is not (see the shape below), so it waits.

perl passes descriptors <= $^F to exec'd children and marks the rest
close-on-exec AT OPEN TIME.  PCL has the $^F box and ignores it: SBCL's
run-program closes every descriptor above 2 in the child, so nothing is ever
inherited.  That is accidentally right for the default ($^F == 2) and wrong
for any program that raises it — which is what run/cloexec.t's six remaining
rows test (the file is DIFF 16/6 since #358).

SIZED ALREADY: sb-ext:run-program :preserve-fds works — measured, for fd >= 4;
fd 3 is used by SBCL's own spawn plumbing and cannot be handed through
(`head -1 <&3` in the child: "Bad file descriptor"; <&4 and <&5 read fine).

SHAPE: mark a descriptor inheritable at open time when fd <= $^F, and pass the
still-open marked ones as :preserve-fds at the ~8 run-program sites.  With the
default $^F the list is always empty, so nothing else can move.

OPEN QUESTION (why this is a task and not a commit): the fd-3 hole needs a
ruling — announce and continue, or refuse?  Rule 12's boundary (effect-only
missing case ANNOUNCES) suggests announce + a not-supported.md line.


RULED s407 (fable-answers-s406.md Â§4.7 ask 4): BEHIND THE RELEASE (a session, not
a filler â ~8 run-program sites + open-time marking).  The fd-3 hole ANNOUNCES
(s329 boundary: an effect, not a value): `PCL: fd 3 cannot be inherited across
exec` on stderr when $^F >= 3 and a spawn happens, with a not-supported.md entry.
subject: cloexec.t's last 6 rows: $^F / fd inheritance across exec is ignored (:preserve-fds works for fd >= 4, fd 3 is SBCL's own plumbing)
